raw_response:
I am 60 now, and I still farm mostly the way that has kept the family steady. I finished middle school, so I do listen to the township technician when he talks about fertilizer split and pest timing, but in the end I still look at my own field and what the neighbors are doing. On my 20 mu, I will keep the main land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the most reliable for grain and cash together. I do not want to gamble too much at my age. But I will still keep some cotton and chili, because if grain price is weak, those can help with income. Since I have a well, I am not afraid of a dry spell, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate carelessly.

This year I would put 10 mu into winter wheat, then the same 10 mu goes straight into summer maize after harvest. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple and fast. I will use a moderate fertilizer rate, not the highest. If I push too hard, I spend more cash up front and may not get it back if weather turns bad. For cotton, I will keep 6 mu because I know how to manage it, though it needs more labor and more spraying. Chili I will keep to 4 mu only, because it makes money if it goes well, but it is fussy and takes labor at harvest. My idea is not to maximize, just to make sure every part of the farm has a role: wheat and maize for stability, cotton and chili for extra cash.
